key_insight: Increasing cavity length-to-depth ratio reduced downstream Stanton number, but at L/D = 6, downstream heat transfer still exceeded the upstream value.
engineering_relevance: Cavity geometry can influence local thermal loads on hypersonic surfaces and should inform thermal-protection design.
method: Tested axisymmetric cavities on a 48° semi-apex-angle cone at Mach 6 in a Ludwieg tunnel.
Varied L/D from 0.5 to 6.0, h/D from −0.25 to 0.5, and Re_D from 23,000 to 74,000.
Combined schlieren and planar laser Rayleigh scattering with surface pressure and heat-transfer measurements.
evidence_signal: Measurements across five L/D values showed decreasing downstream Stanton number with increasing cavity length, while St_d remained above St_u at L/D = 6.
watch_item: The abstract provides no uncertainty estimates or quantitative heat-transfer changes, limiting assessment of design margins.
paper_title: Experimental Investigation of Heat Transfer in Axisymmetric Open Cavities at Hypersonic Speeds
